subject: Private deployment readiness — network & KMS checklist
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@fincap.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment readiness — network & KMS checklist

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to meet the FinCap team. Per our discussion I wanted to capture the follow-up items so we can validate the Private VPC/on-prem option and get you into a Dedicated/private plane design review. Below is a short checklist and next-step timeline. Please reply inline where you can.

Summary of what we heard you need today:
- Private connectivity: you prefer a PrivateLink-style private endpoint over classic peering, but will evaluate peering if we can guarantee stable egress IPs.
- Egress IPs: you need a limited set of static egress IPs for allowlisting with downstream vendors.
- Data residency & KMS: customer-managed keys preferred; SOC2 evidence required.
- Audit & logging: 90-day retention for request & admin logs; SAML + SCIM for SSO.
- Timeline: pilot (5 nodes) targeted in Q4; production rollout early Q1.

Action items for FinCap (please confirm):
1) Share your networking diagram (VPCs/subnets, NAT/egress boxes, Transit Gateway if any) — you mentioned you'll push the diagram to the Drive folder.
2) Confirm whether you want PrivateLink (endpoint service) or VPC Peering as the primary connection path (we can support both but the routing/egress model differs).
3) Send the list of CIDR ranges that must be allowed outbound to third parties (so we can size NAT/egress).
4) Confirm KMS preference: Redwood-hosted vs customer-managed (AWS KMS/HSM).

What Redwood will provide next:
- A short network preflight template for NetOps with required ports, ASNs, and sample route tables.
- An outline of the PrivateLink endpoint setup and the alternative peering flow with egress IP mapping.
- A SOC2 evidence checklist and a draft SLAs/commitments for Dedicated capacity.

Tentative next call: 30 minutes with NetOps + Security to review the preflight (can you do Tue 8/3 morning PT?).

Attachments I expect to receive: fincap-network-diagram.pdf, fincap-privsec-requirements.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll assemble the preflight doc and circulate before the call.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

From: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@fincap.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment readiness — network & KMS checklist

Neha — thanks, this is perfect. We discussed internally and here are answers & the diagram attached.

Quick answers:
- Preferred path: PrivateLink (endpoint) is our first choice due to tenant isolation and easier least-privilege routing. We will only consider peering if PrivateLink introduces unsupported latency for the telemetry stream.
- Egress IPs: we need a set of 4 static outbound IP addresses for allowlisting with our vendors — I attached the current NAT appliance config in the diagram (see fincap-network-diagram.pdf).
- KMS: customer-managed (AWS KMS) is mandatory for production. We need a key rotation policy aligned with our internal compliance.
- Logs: 90-day retention OK; if Redwood can push logs to our S3 bucket via cross-account role that's preferred.

Attachments: fincap-network-diagram.pdf, fincap-privsec-requirements.xlsx (these were uploaded to the Drive link you included).

We can do Tue 8/3 10:00 AM PT for the NetOps call — Alice, Will (IT Ops) and our security lead will join.

Thanks,
Alice Jensen
Head of Infrastructure, FinCap
alice.jensen@fincap.com

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@fincap.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment readiness — network & KMS checklist

Thanks Alice & Neha — I pulled the diagram from Drive and sketched a few clarifying questions for the preflight template (below). I’ll prepare the NetOps checklist so we can run through it on tomorrow’s call.

Marissa’s NetOps clarifying questions (please reply inline):
1) ASN / Transit: Do you run a Transit Gateway with an assigned ASN or are you using a single-VPC NAT gateway? If TGW, please provide the TGW ASN.
2) PrivateLink endpoint subnets: Which AZs do you want endpoints in? We recommend 2 AZs for HA.
3) Egress mapping: The 4 static egress IPs — are they mapped to a pair of NAT routers (2x active/standby) or are they NAT pool addresses? If pool, what is the failover plan?
4) Ports & protocols: We’ll require outbound 443 (TLS) for inference and 9090 for metrics collection (optional). Any additional vendor port requirements?
5) Cross-account S3: For logs to land in your bucket we’ll need a role name to include in the cloudformation we provide (policy will be narrowly scoped).

What we'll bring to the call:
- A 1-page PrivateLink setup checklist (subnet snippets, SG rules, VPC endpoint service owner steps).
- A peering fallback doc showing NAT egress mapping and how we guarantee static egress IPs.
- Sample KMS setup notes for AWS CMKs and rotation considerations.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- 8/3 10:00 AM PT: NetOps + Security call to walk the checklist (30 min) — we’ll record and drop minutes.
- Post-call: We’ll publish the preflight template and an initial implementation estimate for a 5-node pilot.

If that all looks good, I’ll send an invite for 8/3 10:00 AM PT.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

---

From: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@fincap.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment readiness — network & KMS checklist

All good — 8/3 10:00 AM PT works for our team.

Quick inline responses:
1) TGW ASN: 64512 (we use AWS Transit Gateway).
2) AZs: us-west-2a and us-west-2b for endpoints.
3) Egress mapping: 4 IPs are a NAT pool (active-active behind HA appliances) — failover handled by appliance.
4) Ports: 443 and 9090 only; nothing else expected from vendors.
5) Role name for S3: redwood-log-ingest-role-prod (we'll provide the account ID in the drive doc).

I’ve put the appliance config in the Drive folder; see the diagram. Looking forward to the call.

Best,
Alice
